essence: Eusapia, the most pleasure-loving of cities, dug an identical copy of itself underground so that death would be a gentler step; but the dead keep improving their city, the living copy the copy, and in the end no one can tell which Eusapia was the original or who is alive.
textDetails: Eusapia is the city most given to enjoying life and avoiding worry.
To soften the leap from life to death, its people built an exact copy of their city underground.
Corpses are dried so that the skeleton stays wrapped in yellow skin, then carried down to carry on their former activities.
Their carefree moments get priority: most are seated around well-laden tables, set in dancing poses, or made to play little trumpets.
All the trades of the living city operate below as well, or at least those the living practised with more contentment than irritation.
The clockmaker, surrounded by the stopped clocks of his shop, lays his parchment ear against an out-of-tune grandfather clock.
A barber, with a dry brush, soaps the cheekbones of an actor who studies his part with empty eye sockets.
A girl with a laughing skull milks the carcass of a heifer.

Many of the living want a different fate in death: the necropolis teems with big-game hunters, mezzo-sopranos, bankers, violinists, duchesses, courtesans and generals, more than the living city ever had.
A confraternity of hooded brothers escorts the dead below and arranges them where they wished to be; no one else is admitted, and all knowledge of the lower city comes from them.

The same confraternity is said to exist among the dead and to keep doing the job after death; rumour has it that some brothers are already dead yet still go up and down; their authority among the living is vast.

On every trip down the brothers find something new: the dead introduce innovations, not many, but products of sober reflection rather than passing whims, so that year by year the lower city becomes unrecognisable.
Wanting to keep up, the living do whatever the brothers report the dead have adopted, so living Eusapia has begun to copy its own underground copy.
It is said this is nothing new: it was really the dead who built the upper Eusapia, modelled on their own city.
In the twin cities it is no longer possible to tell the living from the dead.
visualConcept: Eusapia is shown as a two-storey world: a floating drum of earth with the living city on its sunlit top and an identical twin city standing upright in a vast candlelit cavern inside it, the two exposed together by a clean wedge-shaped cutaway like an architectural section. Above is a carefree festival town of cream and pastel stucco, striped awnings and bunting: banquet tables round a dance floor, a bandstand of trumpeters, a clock tower, a barber's pole, a dairy yard. Below are the same streets, the same tower and the same tables, occupied by the dried dead with ochre-yellow skin over bone: seated at the banquets, frozen mid-dance, holding little trumpets, practising their favourite trades, the clockmaker with his ear to a grandfather clock among stopped clocks, the barber lathering an actor who reads with empty sockets, a girl milking the skeleton of a heifer. The lower city is visibly more crowded than the upper, thronged with hunters, divas, bankers, violinists, duchesses, courtesans and generals. Four vertical shafts crowned by small striped chapels join the two levels, and hooded brothers in dark robes, with lanterns and litters, are the only traffic between them; one shaft is sliced open by the cutaway so you can watch them descend. The idea reads at a glance: two identical cities, one lit by the sun and one by candles, copying each other through a layer of earth.
layout: Drum: cylinder radius 19, top surface at y 0, rough tapering underside down to y -19; a 100-degree wedge facing the default camera is removed, leaving clean vertical cut faces with umber, ochre and grey strata, pebbles and hanging roots. Cavern: ceiling at y -2.5 (rough, root-hung, 12 hanging lanterns), floor at y -11. Twin city plan, built once and instanced twice (on the surface at y 0 and on the cavern floor at y -11), radius 15: central piazza r 3.5 with 4 banquet tables (3 x 0.6) in a square ring around a round dance floor (r 1.6, 12 dancers) and a bandstand with 4 trumpeters on its north side; clock tower (6 tall) on the north edge; 8 radial streets; about 110 houses of 2-4 storeys (1.2-2.4 wide) with loggias, pergolas and roof terraces, nothing taller than 6.5 so the lower copy clears the cavern ceiling; vignettes near the piazza: the clockmaker (a facade hung with 20 small clock faces, a grandfather clock at the door), the barber (striped pole, chair, seated actor holding a script), the dairy yard (heifer, stool, girl); a small semicircular theatre (r 2) on the east. Four confraternity shafts at r 11, azimuths 45, 135, 225, 315, one lying exactly on a cutaway plane: each a well r 0.8 with a spiral stair, topped on the surface by a small black-and-white striped domed chapel (r 1.2) and opening below through a stone arch. Population: 380 living figures above; 620 dead below (about 1.6 times as many), including 10 hunters, 8 mezzo-sopranos, 10 bankers, 12 violinists, 8 duchesses, 10 courtesans and 8 generals; 12 hooded brothers. Lighting: warm sun above; below, about 60 candle and lantern sources (a few real point lights, the rest emissive sprites).
signatureMotion: 1) The descent: processions of 2-4 hooded brothers carry a wrapped body on a litter from a house to the nearest chapel, wind down the spiral stair inside the shaft (visible in the sliced one) and set the body in its chosen place below, a new seat at a banquet, a new dancer, a new trumpeter; they climb back up carrying a small glowing scroll, the news. Under a few of the hoods the hands are yellow bone. 2) Innovations from below: every 20 s one building of the lower city changes (a roof swells into a small dome, a loggia or pergola sprouts, a tower gains a lantern, a facade changes colour), announced by a candle-gold shimmer; a brother carries a scroll up the nearest shaft; about 8 s later the twin building above makes the same change under a sunlit shimmer. The two cities stay identical, one always a beat behind the other; over a 10-minute cycle the whole skyline changes, then slowly resets. 3) Two festivals on one beat: above, couples whirl on the dance floor, cups lift, trumpets bob and the clock hands turn; below, the same tableau is held still, dancers fixed mid-turn rotating imperceptibly like music-box figures, trumpets raised to lipless mouths, every clock stopped at a different hour, the clockmaker's head bowed against the grandfather clock.
interactionDescription: Inverts which Eusapia is the original. Off: the sunlit city above is solid and the city below follows it. On: the upper city thins into a pale translucent cast with glowing edges, and from every building below a fine gold thread rises straight up through the earth to its twin; along these threads the upper city rebuilds itself storey by storey from the bottom up, made by the dead in the image of their own city. The sunlight above cools to the same candle-amber as the cavern and the living take on the same ochre complexion as the dead, until the two levels can no longer be told apart. Toggling back returns the sun and the upper city's own colours.
mood: Above: a carefree late afternoon at the height of summer, golden and festive, warm haze, bunting stirring, long soft shadows. Below: the same hour by candlelight, amber pools in deep umber shade, dust motes turning in lantern beams, the hush of a ballroom after the music has stopped. The cut earth between them is cool, damp and dark. Gently macabre, more convivial than grim.
caption: Eusapia loves its pleasures too well to give them up at death, so it dug a second Eusapia beneath the first, street for street. The dead, dried inside their yellow skin, are seated at banquets, posed mid-dance, given little trumpets and their favourite trades. Hooded brothers carry them down and bring back word of what has changed, and the city above hurries to follow the fashions below. No one can say any longer which city is the copy.
motto: Below, the dead invent; above, the living imitate.
camera: Facing the cutaway wedge from just above the surface: distance 40 from target (0, -4.5, 0), elevation 16 degrees, field of view 38. The sunlit skyline fills the top third, the cut earth roof is a dark band, the candlelit cavern fills the middle, and the sliced shaft with a descending brother sits near the centre. Orbit limited to +-40 degrees so the cutaway always faces the viewer.
